messages:
Maya: :wave: hey everyone — new hire q. Trying to figure out channel etiquette. Where should I post: laptop/access problems, infra incidents, product feedback, and small design questions? Also bots are spamming me — any quick tips to quiet them?

Omar: welcome, Maya! short version: access/laptop -> #help or DM IT, infra incidents -> #incidents (only urgent outages), product feedback -> #product-feedback, design/help -> DM the designer or #design for async threads. :thumbsup:

Priya: +1 to Omar. For developer/setup questions specifically, use #devex — we triage onboarding/tooling there. If it's a one-off config, DM the person who owned the repo. For recurring Qs, start a thread in #devex so answers are discoverable.

onboard-bot: Welcome Maya! :tada: Your onboarding checklist: 1) Complete SSO and 2FA 2) Join #eng, #devex, #product 3) Run `rwi-setup` on your laptop. Reply "done" to mark items.

Maya: thanks — that helps. small follow-up: when is it okay to @channel vs @here?

Alex: @channel is for company/large-team announcements only. @here is for people online in a channel for time-sensitive asks (use sparingly). If unsure, post in a thread or DM a team lead first. :eyes:

Lina: Practical etiquette we use: 1) Use threads for follow-ups in busy channels. 2) Add context in one sentence + link to PR/issue. 3) For urgent paging use @oncall in #incidents or the paging integration. 4) Huge asks -> post in #eng-sr or schedule a sync.

Maya: got it. about the bots — how do I mute onboarding emails/bot pings without missing important alerts?

Priya: open channel details -> Integrations -> click the bot -> uncheck notifications, or use Slack top-right menu: "Other notifications" -> choose "Triage only". For page-like alerts we keep @oncall enabled so muting other bots is fine.

Alex: also use "Do Not Disturb" windows for deep work. And click the small bell icon on a channel header to mute a channel temporarily.

Maya: sweet, thanks. last Q: first-week posting etiquette — is it ok to post 1-line intros in #general or should I use #introductions?

Omar: post in #introductions — we'll cross-post to #general if it's interesting broadly. In #introductions include: name, role, team, timezone, 1 fun thing. Keep it short. :wave:

Maya: perfect — posting now. appreciate the quick tips! :slightly_smiling_face:
